quantum_risk.rationale: Public-key primitives (RSA, ECC) are vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on a future cryptographically-relevant quantum computer (CRQC). Ciphertext captured today can be decrypted later (Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later), and long-lived signatures forged - which is why PQC migration is time-critical.

migration_impact.reason: RSA-2048 is vulnerable to Shor's algorithm; migrate to NIST FIPS 203 (ML-KEM-768) and FIPS 204 (ML-DSA-65).

suggestions: Replace RSA-2048 with ML-KEM-768 / ML-DSA-65 (CNSA 2.0 / NIST PQC) in 'unknown'.
Adopt hybrid key exchange (X25519MLKEM768) so TLS and message-level handshakes are HNDL-safe today.

waves.name: Wave 1 - Stop the bleeding (HNDL & PQC triage)
waves.focus: Rotate HNDL-exposed keys, add hybrid handshakes and stage urgent post-quantum replacements for publicly exposed primitives.

waves.name: Wave 2 - Post-quantum migration
waves.focus: Systematically move public-key signatures and key exchange to ML-KEM / ML-DSA per CNSA 2.0, covering downstream trust chains.

waves.name: Wave 3 - Hardening & governance
waves.focus: Consolidate symmetric modes (AES-256), strengthen hashes to SHA-3, retire legacy ciphers and codify crypto policy so new failures cannot ship.

executive_summary: The ECDAT Enterprise Post-Quantum Cryptographic Risk Report evaluated a total of 10 cryptographic assets, identifying 6 high-risk configurations and 5 quantum-vulnerable items concentrated within a single internal blast zone. Although zero urgent or critical risk issues were detected immediately, proactive remediation is vital over an estimated 6-quarter timeline. All vulnerable primitives must undergo systematic migration to NIST-approved post-quantum standards according to structured waves.
quantum_risk_narrative: Public-key primitives such as RSA and ECC are fundamentally vulnerable to Shor's algorithm running on a future cryptographically-relevant quantum computer (CRQC). Furthermore, ciphertext captured today remains susceptible to Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later (HNDL) attacks, making timely post-quantum migration an urgent enterprise imperative.

strategic_recommendations.title: Wave 1 - Stop the bleeding (HNDL & PQC triage)
strategic_recommendations.description: Inventory and prioritize all quantum-vulnerable assets within the internal 'unknown' service blast zone, establishing baseline visibility and halting new deployments of legacy algorithms.

strategic_recommendations.title: Wave 2 - Post-quantum migration
strategic_recommendations.description: Execute systematic cryptographic replacements for identified vulnerable public-key and symmetric assets, transitioning to NIST FIPS 203 (ML-KEM) and FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) standards.

strategic_recommendations.title: Wave 3 - Hardening & governance
strategic_recommendations.description: Enforce strict cryptographic governance, continuously audit algorithm usage via automated tooling, and complete long-term hardening across all enterprise services.
